findings.title: add/remove member actions require :group_id but route and client supply :id
findings.body: Admin JS calls PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members.json with only user_id/usernames in the body. The Rails member route `delete/put 'members'` under `resources :groups` supplies the group id as params[:id], not params[:group_id]. Both add_members (line 66) and remove_member (line 85) do Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i), so every real request raises ActionController::ParameterMissing and the admin add/remove member feature is broken. Specs pass only because they call the action directly with group_id, bypassing routing.

findings.title: totalPages off-by-one creates phantom empty page
findings.body: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 instead of ceil. For example 50 members with limit 50 yields 2 pages instead of 1, 100/50 yields 3 instead of 2. Combined with next action capping offset at Math.min(offset+limit, user_count), the UI can navigate to offset == user_count which returns zero members, showing an empty last page and wrong 2/2 or 3/3 counters.

findings.title: Public group members page only loads first page with no pagination
findings.body: The public members route now sets the model to the Group object and calls model.findMembers() once, which defaults to limit 50 offset 0. There is no next/previous UI on the public members template. Previously non-automatic groups returned all members, so any group with more than 50 members now permanently shows only the first 50 with no way to see the rest.

findings.title: Unbounded limit/offset params allow DoS and invalid queries
findings.body: Members action does limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i and offset = params[:offset].to_i with no clamping. A caller can request limit=1000000 to force loading huge numbers of users into memory, or negative limit/offset which produces SQL errors or surprising results. Limit should be clamped to a sane max (e.g. 1..200) and offset to >=0.

findings.title: Group create ignores alias_level sent by client
findings.body: The JS Group.asJSON() sends name, alias_level and visible, and update handles alias_level, but create only assigns name and visible. A group created with a non-default alias level silently loses that choice and gets the default, requiring a second update to fix.

findings.title: Adding members splits on comma without stripping whitespace
findings.body: add_members does usernames.split(',').each with no strip. Input like 'alice, bob' from a user-selector leaves a leading space on the second name, so User.find_by_username(' bob') returns nil and that user is silently skipped while the endpoint still returns success. The admin thinks all users were added when only a subset was.

findings.title: remove_member uses low-level association delete bypassing domain logic
findings.body: remove_member does group.users.delete(user_id) while the add path uses group.add(user) and the old code used group.remove(user). Direct association delete bypasses Group model callbacks and counter maintenance, then calls group.save redundantly. This risks stale user_count and missed side effects, and is inconsistent with the add path.

findings.title: remove_member automatic-group test uses wrong HTTP verb
findings.body: The test for cannot remove members from automatic groups does xhr :put, :remove_member while the route is DELETE members => remove_member. Controller specs invoke the action directly regardless of verb, so the test passes while masking that a real PUT would not route and that the controller/route :group_id vs :id mismatch is not exercised. It gives false confidence for the member-removal endpoint.
